title: Gate trace-matrix input (v0)
description: Gate's OWN minimal shape for a requirement->test traceability matrix (TzolkinB/skills#199, ADR-0045) — not a copy of any external tool's internal format. TEA's `trace` workflow (bmad-testarch-trace, MIT-licensed, BMad Code LLC) is the reference producer: its step-03 marks each requirement FULL/PARTIAL/NONE by mapping matching tests identified by stable identity fields (id/title/file/line), and step-05 writes a gate-decision.json with p0_status/p1_status/overall_status. This schema deliberately does NOT ingest TEA's internal JSON verbatim (orchestrate-don't-couple) — a separate adapter (`tea-to-trace-matrix.mjs`, #220/ADR-0050) converts a `trace` run into this shape, one row per requirement, each `tests[]` entry a `<file>::<title>` string matching the join key gate-audit-test/v0.3's `runs[].test` already uses. That adapter reads TEA's step-04 Phase-1 coverage-matrix JSON (the only `trace` artifact carrying per-requirement rows AND per-test titles; its path is recorded in traceability-matrix.md's frontmatter as `tempCoverageMatrixPath`) — never traceability-matrix.md's body, whose Detailed Mapping section identifies tests as `id` - file:line with no title, and never e2e-trace-summary.json / gate-decision.json, which carry aggregates and a gate signal only. TEA's coverage vocabulary is five-valued; UNIT-ONLY and INTEGRATION-ONLY convert to PARTIAL (never FULL — a conversion may not widen the producer's own presence call). Gate reads this file only to JOIN it against an audit-test emission (three-state rollup per requirement); it never persists or accumulates a matrix of its own.

gateStatus.description: OPTIONAL passthrough of the producing tool's own categorical gate (e.g. TEA step-05's gate_status) — informational only, displayed for cross-reference, NEVER read to derive Gate's own business-risk rollup or the ship/canary/hold decision.

requirements.description: One row per requirement/criterion the matrix covers. An empty array is valid (a matrix that legitimately covers nothing) — Gate never synthesizes a row to fill the table.

id.description: requirement/criterion identifier, e.g. "REQ-12" or an endpoint/spec-item name

status.description: the producing tool's own PRESENCE verdict — a test exists (or doesn't) for this requirement. Gate never overrides this; it only adds a credibility read on TOP of a FULL/PARTIAL row.

tests.description: matched test identifiers, `<spec-file>::<test title>` — the same join key `gate-audit-test/v0.3`'s `runs[].test` uses. MUST be empty when status is NONE, and MUST be non-empty when status is FULL or PARTIAL (INGEST GUARD: a row violating this is arithmetically impossible — the whole matrix is rejected, never silently accepted, same treatment as an inconsistent audit-test tally).

$comment: INGEST GUARDS (mirrors gate-audit-test/v0.3's ingest guards): `schema` is matched EXACTLY, never a prefix. Every requirement `id` must be unique within the matrix (a duplicate is rejected — same 'never trust a model's counts blind' posture). `tests.length === 0` iff `status === 'NONE'` is enforced both ways. Gate's join (`resolveBusinessRisk`) then buckets each FULL/PARTIAL row into one of three states by looking up its `tests[]` against an audit-test emission's `runs[]` (the execution-confirmed subset only): `mutation-proven` (every mapped test appears as `killed`), `hollow` (any mapped test appears as `survived` — worst-wins, this beats mutation-proven), `unverified` (the default — includes a test with no `runs[]` record at all, i.e. never deep-audited, likely-hollow, or baseline-lock). A `status:'NONE'` row has no test to check and is reported separately as `not-covered`, never folded into the three-state count — that gap is the producing tool's own presence read, not this join's to invent evidence for.
